- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude.ai Figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md

## claude.ai Zapier
This server connects you to 9,000+ apps via Zapier.

IMPORTANT: Before calling any tool, ensure you have loaded the available tools from this server (tools/list).

If the user seems new or has no tools enabled, retrieve the "zapier:onboarding" skill using get_zapier_skill and follow its instructions.
Use list_zapier_skills to discover other saved workflows.

## Managing what's enabled

- `inspect_zapier_actions({ selected_api?, action?, tool_name?, params? })` — inspect enabled actions and resolve action parameter schemas. **Returns everything you need to build an execute call**: each action's `app` (display name), `selected_api`, `action` key, `action_type` (exact SDK type), `tool_name`, `params`, inline dynamic enum values when resolvable, and `dynamic_properties_schema` when parent values in `params` are sufficient.
- `discover_zapier_actions({ app? })` — search the Zapier app catalog for actions to enable (`app` is a free-text search query).
- `enable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — add an action (you'll receive a `tools/list_changed` notification afterwards). Pass the `selected_api` returned by `discover_zapier_actions`.
- `disable_zapier_action({ selected_api, app_display_name?, action? })` — remove an action. Pass the `selected_api` from `inspect_zapier_actions`.

## Executing an action

Always call `inspect_zapier_actions` first to retrieve the action's exact `selected_api`, `action` key, `tool_name`, parameter schema, and any dynamic-argument guidance. Then:

1. If a parameter has `dynamic_enum_values`, use one of those `value` fields. If it has `dynamic_enum_missing_dependencies` or no usable value yet, set the dependency params you know and call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` again. Use `enum_property`, `enum_search`, and `enum_cursor` with the same tool when you need to search or page one dynamic enum.
2. If the action includes `dynamic_properties_depends_on`, settle those parameters' values, then call `inspect_zapier_actions({ tool_name, params })` agai… [truncated]

## fossa
Read-only access to FOSSA projects, revisions, dependencies, licensing issues, vulnerability issues, quality issues, and attribution reports. No tool mutates FOSSA state.

Use when asked to implement an API as an MCP server, wrap a REST API in MCP tools, add tool coverage for new endpoints to an existing MCP server, plan API-to-tool parity, or discover undocumented API usage behind a web interface.

Use when asked to mitigate, compensate for, or "protect against" CVEs found by FOSSA, to write WAF sensors/rules for a project's dependencies, or whenever FOSSA findings and NeuVector need to be connected. Also use when asked to review or roll back sensors created this way.

80	`Discover → Protect` moves landed, both dimensions, including with the other

85	- **The write path has never run against a service with live members.** All tool-level

104	   vulnerability suppression bypass it.

110	- **`NV_ALLOW_NODE_EXEC`?** `nv_set_custom_compliance_checks` ships shell scripts the
111	  privileged enforcer runs on every node. The confirm token binds the script bytes,
112	  but in an agent loop the same model writes and confirms. Proposed: deploy-time flag
113	  defaulting off, checked in the guard like `read_only`. Not built.
114	- **Revive `feat/config-transfer`?** Still undecided; self-contained and droppable.
115	- Should the tool-level write path be exercised once against a service with members
116	  before it is trusted for a real workload?
117

119	
120	1. lab-memory repo: pin `mcp==1.28.1` in its manifests — cluster patch is live but not in git.
121	2. `lab-memory` WAF sensors never created; re-run `/fossa-protect` fresh.
122	3. `ollama-code-mcp` repo manifest still pins mcp 1.6.0 (deliberate).
123	4. Ticket board `agent-tools.py doctor --fix` review (deprioritized).
124	5. `config._env("")` xfail; E501 ignore; iam_read/iam_write fold — cosmetic.
125	6. Do NOT add neuvector-mcp to Fleet until the user says so.
126	7. Merged branches still local: `feat/full-write-surface`, `fix/waf-omitempty-fields`,
127	   `fix/service-policy-mode`, `feat/waf-tools-and-workload-fix`, `build/phases-1-11`.
128	
129	## Gotchas worth knowing
130	
131	- **Never trust `status: "applied"` — and never trust one immediate read either.**
132	  The second half is the new lesson. Use a bounded retry; that is what
133	  `verify_applied()` does (8 × 0.5s, returns on first clean read).
134	- **Never `kubectl apply -f deploy/deployment.yaml`** — `REPLACE_ME` placeholders in
135	  the Secrets. Use `kubectl set image`.
136	- **The build Job clones `main` from GitHub**, so a version bump must be merged
137	  *before* the build runs or the image reports the old version.
138	- **Ship sequence that works:** bump version on `main` → `kubectl apply -f
139	  deploy/build-job.yaml` (kaniko, namespace `ai`, node `sdf1`, ~60s) → `kubectl set
140	  image` → `kubectl rollout status`.
141	- **`kubectl get pod ... -o jsonpath='{.items[0]...}'` can pick the terminating pod**
142	  during a rollout. Use `-o 'custom-columns=...'` (quoted — zsh globs the bare form).
143	- **MCP clients re-list tools only on reconnect.** After a roll, the old signature
144	  persists until `/mcp`. The pod log line `nv.connected` is authoritative.
145	- **To drive the shipped server in-pod:** `kubectl exec -i ... -- python3 -` with a
146	  script that sets `NV_TRANSPORT=stdio` then uses `fastmcp.Client(build_server())`.
147	  For raw wire probing, `httpx` + `X-Auth-Apikey: <access>:<secret>` from pod env,
148	  `verify=False`. Container is named **`server`**.
149	- **Spec gate R6 regex needs punctuation immediately after the path** in a
150	  `Calls <METHOD> <path>` line — `Calls GET /v1/service to read...` does NOT match;
151	  `Calls GET /v1/service, to read...` does. Silent until `make spec` fails.
152	- **This repo lives in iCloud Drive.** Run `find . -name "* 2.*"` before any `git add -A`.
153	- Reading the `harbor-pull` secret from the shell is blocked by the permission
154	  classifier. Mount it into a pod instead.
155	- Scratchpad probe scripts from this session (`verify_1_1_1.py`, `probe_latency.py`,
156	  `probe_confirm.py`) are session-temp and will be gone; the method is described above.

Report on:

1. Where `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` is defined/parsed (likely src/neuvector_mcp/config.py) — its exact type. Is it a single string, a list, a set? What does it default to? What happens when unset/empty?

2. The guard module (likely src/neuvector_mcp/guard.py or similar) — find the function(s) that check namespace scope. Give me exact function names, signatures, and file:line. How does a tool opt in to the namespace check? Is it a decorator, an explicit call, a parameter on a registration helper?

3. CRITICAL: enumerate which tools DO and DO NOT go through the namespace check. Specifically confirm the status of `nv_apply_system_request` and any cluster-wide vulnerability suppression tool (search tools/vulnerability_write.py). Are they genuinely unchecked? Quote the relevant code.

4. Is there any existing notion of "cluster-wide" or a wildcard value in the namespace handling? Any TODO/FIXME comments about it?

5. How is the guard tested? Point me at the relevant test files and the names of tests covering namespace scoping.

content.text:
Here is the map.

## 1. Definition and parsing of `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`

**Type: `tuple[str, ...]`, defaulting to `()` (empty tuple).**

- `/Users/rashford/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/neuvector-mcp/src/neuvector_mcp/config.py:126` — field declaration on the frozen pydantic `Settings` model (`model_config = {"frozen": True, "extra": "forbid"}`, line 95):
  ```python
  allowed_namespaces: tuple[str, ...] = ()
  ```
- `config.py:234-236` — parsing in `load_settings()`:
  ```python
  allowed_namespaces=tuple(
      n.strip() for n in (_env("ALLOWED_NAMESPACES", "") or "").split(",") if n.strip()
  ),
  ```
- `_env` (`config.py:67-74`) reads `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`, falling back to the contents of `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES_FILE`. An empty-string env var is treated as unset.
- Unset/empty → `()`. Comma-split, whitespace-stripped, empty elements dropped. **No field_validator on this field** — no case normalisation, no wildcard expansion, no dedup, no validation that the namespaces exist.
- Empty tuple is falsy, and the guard short-circuits on it (see §2), so **unset = no namespace enforcement at all** (fail-open by design).

## 2. The guard

`/Users/rashford/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/neuvector-mcp/src/neuvector_mcp/guard.py`

There is exactly **one** function, and the namespace check is **not** a decorator and **not** a registration-helper parameter — it is an *optional keyword argument each tool must remember to pass*:

- `guard.py:48-58` — signature:
  ```python
  def authorise_write(
      settings: Settings, *, operation: str, toolset: str, target: str,
      effect: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None, confirm: str | None,
      namespace: str | None = None,
  ) -> WriteOutcome | None:
  ```
- `guard.py:90-94` — the entire namespace enforcement:
  ```python
  if namespace and settings.allowed_namespaces and namespace not in settings.allowed_namespaces:
      raise GuardError(
          f"{operation} targets namespace {namespace!r}, which is outside "
          f"NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES ({sorted(settings.allowed_namespaces)})."
      )

"""Write guard: the only place a mutating call may be authorised.

Every mutating tool calls :func:`authorise_write` before it touches the client.
The guard enforces four independent conditions, in this order:

1. ``NV_READ_ONLY`` must be false.
2. The tool's toolset must be enabled in ``NV_TOOLSETS``.
3. When ``NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES`` is non-empty, the target namespace must be in it.
4. When ``NV_REQUIRE_CONFIRM_TOKEN`` is true, the caller must echo back a
   deterministic confirmation token derived from the exact operation.

Condition 4 makes accidental writes structurally impossible: the model cannot
guess the token, so it must first call the tool without one, read the returned
plan, and call again with the token. That two-step handshake is the audit trail.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
from collections.abc import Mapping
from typing import Any

from .config import Settings
from .errors import GuardError
from .models import WriteOutcome


def confirm_token(operation: str, target: str, payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> str:
    """Derive the confirmation token for one specific mutation.

    The token is a function of the operation name, the target identifier and the
    canonical JSON form of the payload, so changing any field invalidates it.

    Args:
        operation: Stable operation id, e.g. ``"nv_delete_group"``.
        target: The object this mutation acts on, e.g. ``"nv.prod.api"``.
        payload: Request body, or ``None`` for payload-free operations.

    Returns:
        A 12-character lowercase hex token.
    """
    canonical = json.dumps(payload or {}, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    digest = hashlib.sha256(f"{operation}|{target}|{canonical}".encode()).hexdigest()
    return digest[:12]


def authorise_write(
    settings: Settings,
    *,
    operation: str,
    toolset: str,
    target: str,
    effect: str,
    payload: Mapping[str, Any] | None,
    confirm: str | None,
    namespace: str | None = None,
) -> WriteOutcome | None:
    """Decide whether one mutating call may proceed.

    Args:
        settings: Active server settings.
        operation: Tool name, used in the token and the audit record.
        toolset: The tool's toolset tag, e.g. ``"policy_write"``.
        target: Human-readable identifier of the object being changed.
        effect: One-sentence description of what will change, for the plan.
        payload: The exact body that will be sent to the controller.
        confirm: Token supplied by the caller, or ``None`` on the first call.
        namespace: Namespace the change lands in, when the operation is scoped.

    Returns:
        ``None`` when the caller may proceed, or a
        :class:`~neuvector_mcp.models.WriteOutcome` with
        ``status="confirmation_required"`` that the tool must return verbatim.

    Raises:
        GuardError: when the operation is forbidden outright, or when the
            supplied token does not match.
    """
    if settings.read_only:
        raise GuardError(
            f"{operation} is a mutating operation and this server is running with "
            "NV_READ_ONLY=true. No request was sent to the controller."
        )
    if not settings.toolset_enabled(toolset):
        raise GuardError(
            f"{operation} belongs to toolset {toolset!r}, which is not enabled. "
            f"Enabled toolsets: {sorted(settings.toolsets)}."
        )
    if namespace and settings.allowed_namespaces and namespace not in settings.allowed_namespaces:
        raise GuardError(
            f"{operation} targets namespace {namespace!r}, which is outside "
            f"NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES ({sorted(settings.allowed_namespaces)})."
        )

    expected = confirm_token(operation, target, payload)
    if not settings.require_confirm_token:
        return None
    if confirm is None:
        return WriteOutcome(
            status="confirmation_required",
            operation=operation,
            target=target,
            effect=effect,
            payload=dict(payload or {}),
            confirm_token=expected,
            next_step=(
                f"Review 'effect' and 'payload'. To execute, call {operation} again "
                f"with identical arguments plus confirm={expected!r}."
            ),
        )
    if confirm != expected:
        raise GuardError(
            f"confirm token mismatch for {operation} on {target!r}. The arguments "
            "changed since the token was issued. Call again without 'confirm' to "
            "get a fresh plan and token."
        )
    return None

"""Configuration for the NeuVector MCP server.

All configuration is supplied through environment variables prefixed ``NV_``.
Nothing is read from the filesystem except the optional ``*_FILE`` indirections,
which exist so Kubernetes Secrets can be mounted as files instead of env vars.

This module has no dependencies on any other module in this package.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, field_validator, model_validator

Transport = Literal["stdio", "http"]
AuthMode = Literal["apikey", "password"]

#: Tool tags that may be enabled via ``NV_TOOLSETS``.
ALL_TOOLSETS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    # read-only toolsets
    "inventory",
    "vulnerability",
    "compliance",
    "events",
    "policy_read",
    "iam_read",
    # mutating toolsets
    "policy_write",
    "admission",
    "scan_ops",
    "runtime_ops",
    "iam_write",

def _entry_namespace(entry: VulnerabilityProfileEntryInput) -> NamespaceScope:
    """Scope to hand the guard for NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES.

    An entry with no namespaces suppresses the CVE everywhere, which is broader
    than any allowlist entry could authorise, so it reports as CLUSTER_WIDE. An
    entry pinned to several namespaces reports all of them: gating only the
    single-namespace case would mean naming *more* namespaces bought *less*
    enforcement.
    """
    return tuple(entry.namespaces) if entry.namespaces else CLUSTER_WIDE


def _entries_namespace(entries: Sequence[VulnerabilityProfileEntryInput]) -> NamespaceScope:
    """Combined scope of a whole-profile replace.

    The replace drops any entry it does not restate, so its reach is the union of
    the entries it carries — and cluster-wide the moment any one of them is.
    """
    if any(not entry.namespaces for entry in entries):
        return CLUSTER_WIDE
    return tuple(sorted({ns for entry in entries for ns in entry.namespaces}))

async def test_first_call_returns_plan_and_sends_nothing(client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter) -> None:
    route = nv_mock.patch(PATCH_SERVICE_CONFIG).respond(200, json={})
    result = await client.call_tool(
        "nv_set_group_policy_mode", {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Protect"}

import json

import pytest

from neuvector_mcp.config import DEFAULT_TOOLSETS
from neuvector_mcp.guard import confirm_token

pytestmark = pytest.mark.asyncio

PATCH_SERVICE_CONFIG = "/v1/service/config"


async def test_first_call_returns_plan_and_sends_nothing(client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter) -> None:
    route = nv_mock.patch(PATCH_SERVICE_CONFIG).respond(200, json={})
    result = await client.call_tool(
        "nv_set_group_policy_mode", {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Protect"}
    )
    body = result.structured_content
    assert body["status"] == "confirmation_required"
    assert len(body["confirm_token"]) == 12
    assert "blocked immediately" in body["effect"]
    assert route.call_count == 0, "the guard must not touch the controller"


async def test_confirmed_call_applies(client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter) -> None:
    fake = FakeServices({"api.prod": {"policy_mode": "Monitor"}}).install(nv_mock)
    args = {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Protect"}
    plan = await client.call_tool("nv_set_group_policy_mode", args)
    token = plan.structured_content["confirm_token"]

    result = await client.call_tool("nv_set_group_policy_mode", {**args, "confirm": token})
    assert result.structured_content["status"] == "applied"
    assert fake.writes.call_count == 1
    assert json.loads(fake.writes.calls.last.request.read()) == {
        "config": {"services": ["api.prod"], "policy_mode": "Protect"}
    }
    assert fake.mode("api.prod") == "Protect"


async def test_confirmed_call_survives_the_controller_write_lag(
    client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter
) -> None:
    """The controller acknowledges before the change is readable; that is not a failure."""
    fake = FakeServices({"api.prod": {"policy_mode": "Discover"}}, lag_reads=3).install(nv_mock)
    args = {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Protect"}
    plan = await client.call_tool("nv_set_group_policy_mode", args)

    result = await client.call_tool(
        "nv_set_group_policy_mode",
        {**args, "confirm": plan.structured_content["confirm_token"]},
    )

    assert fake.patches == [{"services": ["api.prod"], "policy_mode": "Protect"}]
    assert fake.mode("api.prod") == "Protect"
    assert "Discover -> Protect" in result.structured_content["effect"]
    assert fake.writes.call_count == 1, "the write is not retried, only the read"


async def test_confirmed_call_refuses_to_claim_a_dropped_change(
    client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter
) -> None:
    fake = FakeServices({"api.prod": {"policy_mode": "Discover"}}, apply_writes=False).install(
        nv_mock
    )
    args = {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Monitor"}
    plan = await client.call_tool("nv_set_group_policy_mode", args)

    with pytest.raises(Exception) as excinfo:
        await client.call_tool(
            "nv_set_group_policy_mode",
            {**args, "confirm": plan.structured_content["confirm_token"]},
        )

    assert "did not take" in str(excinfo.value)
    assert fake.writes.call_count == 1


async def test_confirmed_call_on_an_unknown_service_writes_nothing(
    client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter
) -> None:
    fake = FakeServices({"api.prod": {"policy_mode": "Discover"}}).install(nv_mock)
    args = {"group_name": "nv.typo.prod", "mode": "Monitor"}
    plan = await client.call_tool("nv_set_group_policy_mode", args)

    with pytest.raises(Exception) as excinfo:
        await client.call_tool(
            "nv_set_group_policy_mode",
            {**args, "confirm": plan.structured_content["confirm_token"]},
        )

    assert "no service named" in str(excinfo.value)
    assert fake.writes.call_count == 0


async def test_confirmed_call_at_target_sends_no_write(client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter) -> None:
    fake = FakeServices({"api.prod": {"policy_mode": "Protect"}}).install(nv_mock)
    args = {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Protect"}
    plan = await client.call_tool("nv_set_group_policy_mode", args)

    result = await client.call_tool(
        "nv_set_group_policy_mode",
        {**args, "confirm": plan.structured_content["confirm_token"]},
    )

    assert result.structured_content["status"] == "applied"
    assert "no change" in result.structured_content["effect"]
    assert fake.writes.call_count == 0


async def test_custom_group_is_rejected_without_controller_call(
    client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter
) -> None:
    route = nv_mock.patch(PATCH_SERVICE_CONFIG).respond(200, json={})
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as excinfo:
        await client.call_tool(
            "nv_set_group_policy_mode", {"group_name": "custom-group", "mode": "Protect"}
        )
    assert "not a learned group" in str(excinfo.value)
    assert route.call_count == 0


async def test_token_is_bound_to_arguments(client, nv_mock: respx.MockRouter) -> None:
    nv_mock.patch(PATCH_SERVICE_CONFIG).respond(200, json={})
    monitor_token = confirm_token(
        "nv_set_group_policy_mode",
        "nv.api.prod",
        {"config": {"services": ["api.prod"], "policy_mode": "Monitor"}},
    )
    with pytest.raises(Exception) as excinfo:
        await client.call_tool(
            "nv_set_group_policy_mode",
            {"group_name": "nv.api.prod", "mode": "Protect", "confirm": monitor_token},
        )
    assert "confirm token mismatch" in str(excinfo.value)

def _authorise(namespace, **settings_kw):
    """Call the guard directly with confirmation off; returns None when permitted."""
    return authorise_write(
        make_settings(require_confirm_token=False, **settings_kw),
        operation="nv_probe",
        toolset="policy_write",
        target="probe",
        effect="probe",
        payload=None,
        confirm=None,
        namespace=namespace,
    )


def test_scope_sequence_requires_every_namespace_inside_allowlist() -> None:
    assert _authorise(("staging", "dev"), allowed_namespaces=("staging", "dev")) is None

    with pytest.raises(GuardError) as excinfo:
        _authorise(("staging", "prod"), allowed_namespaces=("staging", "dev"))
    # Naming more namespaces must not buy less enforcement: the one outside decides.
    assert "['prod']" in str(excinfo.value)


def test_cluster_wide_is_refused_when_an_allowlist_is_set() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(GuardError) as excinfo:
        _authorise(CLUSTER_WIDE, allowed_namespaces=("staging",))
    assert "cluster-wide" in str(excinfo.value)
    assert "NV_ALLOW_CLUSTER_WIDE" in str(excinfo.value)


def test_cluster_wide_is_permitted_when_opted_into() -> None:
    assert (
        _authorise(CLUSTER_WIDE, allowed_namespaces=("staging",), allow_cluster_wide=True) is None
    )


def test_cluster_wide_is_unrestricted_without_an_allowlist() -> None:
    """No allowlist means no expressed intent to scope, so nothing changes."""
    assert _authorise(CLUSTER_WIDE) is None
    assert _authorise(CLUSTER_WIDE, allowed_namespaces=()) is None


def test_none_scope_is_never_blocked() -> None:
    """None means the object has no namespace dimension, not 'scope unknown'."""
    assert _authorise(None, allowed_namespaces=("staging",)) is None


def test_namespace_argument_is_required() -> None:
    """The permissive case must not be reachable by forgetting an argument."""
    with pytest.raises(TypeError):
        authorise_write(  # type: ignore[call-arg]
            make_settings(),
            operation="nv_probe",
            toolset="policy_write",
            target="probe",
            effect="probe",

    nv_mock: respx.MockRouter,
) -> None:
    """The former gap, now closed.

    POST /v1/system/request carries no namespace, so the allowlist cannot narrow
    this call - but that makes it broader than anything the allowlist authorises,
    not exempt from it. The guard marks it CLUSTER_WIDE and refuses.

    route = nv_mock.post(SYSTEM_REQUEST_PATH).respond(200, json={})
    server = build_server(make_settings(allowed_namespaces=("staging",)))
    async with Client(server) as client:

            await _confirmed(client, "nv_apply_system_request", {"policy_mode": "Protect"})

### Safety model

Five independent layers. A mutation must clear all five.

```
 1. Transport auth ── HTTP requires a bearer token; stdio inherits process trust
 2. Controller RBAC ─ the API key's NeuVector role is the real ceiling
 3. NV_READ_ONLY ──── mutating toolsets are not registered at all
 4. NV_TOOLSETS ───── unenabled toolsets are absent from tools/list
 5. Confirm token ─── per-operation, payload-bound, two-step handshake
```

Layer 2 is the one that actually protects the cluster. The other four protect
against model error, not against a compromised credential.

---

## The confirmation handshake

Every mutating tool takes an optional `confirm` argument. Call it once **without**

Layer 2 is the one that actually protects the cluster. The other four protect
against model error, not against a compromised credential.

### Cluster-wide mutations

`NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` narrows mutations to a set of namespaces, but some
mutations have no namespace to narrow: `nv_apply_system_request` moves every
service in the cluster, `nv_delete_all_network_rules` empties the whole ruleset,
a vulnerability profile entry with no `namespaces` suppresses a CVE everywhere.

Such an operation is **broader** than anything the allowlist could authorise, so
the guard refuses it whenever an allowlist is set rather than waving it through
for lack of a namespace to check. `NV_ALLOW_CLUSTER_WIDE=true` re-permits it.

Three scopes exist, and every mutating tool declares one explicitly:

| Scope | Meaning | Under an allowlist |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one or more namespaces | the mutation names where it lands | every name must be in the list |
| cluster-wide | the mutation cannot be confined | refused unless `NV_ALLOW_CLUSTER_WIDE=true` |
| none | the object has no namespace dimension (a sensor definition, a registry) | always permitted |

With no allowlist set there is no expressed intent to scope, so cluster-wide
mutations behave exactly as they always have.

---

### D.0.5 Namespace enforcement when the target has no namespace in its name

`authorise_write(namespace=...)` takes **one** namespace and is the only place
`NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` is enforced (SPEC 6, layer 5). Three shapes occur here:

| Shape | Tools | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Namespace is derivable from the target name | `nv_set_service_mode` (service names are `<service>.<namespace>`), `nv_set_namespace_tags` (the target **is** the namespace) | derive it and pass it |
| Target is an opaque id | `nv_quarantine_workload`, `nv_start_packet_capture`, `nv_trigger_scan(target='workload')` | the tool takes an explicit `namespace` argument. **Required** for the two `runtime_ops` tools, optional for the scan. It is used for the guard check only and is **never sent to the controller**. |
| Cluster-wide, no namespace | `nv_update_system_config`, `nv_update_scan_config`, registry and IAM tools, host/registry scans, bench runs | pass `namespace=None`. `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` cannot scope a cluster-wide change; say so in Notes. |

input.new_string:
`authorise_write(namespace=...)` is the only place `NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES` is
enforced (SPEC 6, layer 5). The argument is **required**: a tool that omits it
would otherwise land in the most permissive case by accident. It accepts a name,
a sequence of names, `CLUSTER_WIDE`, or `None`. Four shapes occur here:

| Shape | Tools | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| Namespace is derivable from the target name | `nv_set_service_mode` (service names are `<service>.<namespace>`), `nv_set_namespace_tags` (the target **is** the namespace) | derive it and pass it |
| Target is an opaque id | `nv_quarantine_workload`, `nv_start_packet_capture`, `nv_trigger_scan(target='workload')` | the tool takes an explicit `namespace` argument. **Required** for the two `runtime_ops` tools, optional for the scan. It is used for the guard check only and is **never sent to the controller**. |
| Several namespaces | batch tools, vulnerability profile entries carrying a `domains` list | pass the whole sequence. Every name must be inside the allowlist — gating only the single-namespace case would mean naming *more* namespaces bought *less* enforcement. |
| Cluster-wide | `nv_apply_system_request`, `nv_update_system_config`, `nv_update_scan_config`, `nv_set_namespace_defaults`, `nv_delete_all_*`, `nv_set_admission_state`, and any suppression with no namespaces | pass `CLUSTER_WIDE`. Such a change is **broader** than the allowlist, not exempt from it: the guard refuses it whenever an allowlist is set unless `NV_ALLOW_CLUSTER_WIDE=true`. Say so in Notes. |

`None` is reserved for an object with genuinely **no namespace dimension** — a
sensor definition, a registry, a webhook, an IAM user. It is never a stand-in
for "scope unknown"; where the reach is unknown but could be the whole cluster
(deleting a rule by opaque id), pass `CLUSTER_WIDE`.

---
# Namespace: deploy alongside NeuVector but not inside it, so a NeuVector
# upgrade never touches this workload.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  labels:
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce: restricted
    pod-security.kubernetes.io/audit: restricted
---
# Controller credentials. Create the API key in NeuVector first:
#   Settings -> API Keys -> Add, role "reader" for read-only deployments.
# Replace both values, or better: manage this Secret with SOPS / External Secrets
# and never commit plaintext.
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  access-key: REPLACE_ME
  secret-key: REPLACE_ME
---
# Bearer tokens that MCP clients present. Format:
#   <token>:<scope>|<scope>,<token2>:<scope>
# Generate with: openssl rand -hex 32
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-clients
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
type: Opaque
stringData:
  bearer-tokens: "REPLACE_ME_32_BYTE_HEX:nv:read"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp-config
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
data:
  NV_CONTROLLER_URL: "https://neuvector-svc-controller-api.cattle-neuvector-system.svc:10443"
  NV_VERIFY_TLS: "false"          # controller serves a self-signed cert by default
  NV_AUTH_MODE: "apikey"
  NV_TRANSPORT: "http"
  NV_HTTP_PATH: "/mcp"
  # Write-capable. Every mutating tool still needs the two-step confirm-token
  # handshake below, which is what makes this safe rather than the read-only flag.
  # Flip NV_READ_ONLY to "true" for a deployment that must never write, and cut
  # NV_TOOLSETS back to the five read toolsets to match.
  NV_READ_ONLY: "false"
  NV_TOOLSETS: "inventory,vulnerability,compliance,events,policy_read,policy_write,scan_ops,runtime_ops"
  NV_REQUIRE_CONFIRM_TOKEN: "true"
  NV_MAX_ITEMS: "200"
  NV_MAX_RESPONSE_CHARS: "60000"
  NV_LOG_LEVEL: "INFO"
  NV_LOG_FORMAT: "json"
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
    spec:
      automountServiceAccountToken: false
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        runAsUser: 10001
        runAsGroup: 10001
        seccompProfile:
          type: RuntimeDefault
      containers:
        - name: server
          # Built in-cluster by deploy/build-job.yaml, which clones main from
          # GitHub and pushes here. Bump both together.
          image: registry.ash4d.com/ash4d-lab/neuvector-mcp:1.1.2
          imagePullPolicy: IfNotPresent
          envFrom:
            - configMapRef:
                name: neuvector-mcp-config
          env:
            - name: NV_API_ACCESS_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
                  key: access-key
            - name: NV_API_SECRET_KEY
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-controller
                  key: secret-key
            - name: NV_HTTP_BEARER_TOKENS
              valueFrom:
                secretKeyRef:
                  name: neuvector-mcp-clients
                  key: bearer-tokens
          ports:
            - name: mcp
              containerPort: 8080
          # The MCP endpoint requires a bearer token, so an unauthenticated HTTP
          # probe would always fail. Probe the socket instead.
          startupProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: mcp }
            failureThreshold: 30
            periodSeconds: 2
          livenessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: mcp }
            periodSeconds: 20
          readinessProbe:
            tcpSocket: { port: mcp }
            periodSeconds: 10
          resources:
            requests: { cpu: 50m, memory: 128Mi }
            limits:   { cpu: 500m, memory: 512Mi }
          securityContext:
            allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
            readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
            capabilities:
              drop: ["ALL"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: tmp
              mountPath: /tmp
      volumes:
        - name: tmp
          emptyDir: {}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  selector:
    app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  ports:
    - name: mcp
      port: 8080
      targetPort: mcp
---
# Egress to the controller and DNS only. Nothing else, in or out.
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: neuvector-mcp
  namespace: neuvector-mcp
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app.kubernetes.io/name: neuvector-mcp
  policyTypes: [Ingress, Egress]
  ingress:
    - ports:
        - port: 8080
          protocol: TCP
  egress:
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: cattle-neuvector-system
      ports:
        - port: 10443
          protocol: TCP
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              kubernetes.io/metadata.name: kube-system
      ports:
        - port: 53
          protocol: UDP
        - port: 53
          protocol: TCP

) -> None:
    """An entry with no namespaces hides the CVE everywhere, which is the wider case.

cd ~/Developer/neuvector-mcp && git commit -q -F - <<'MSG' && git log --oneline -1
Close the NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES cluster-wide bypass

The allowlist could be escaped by operations that were BROADER than any
namespace it could name. authorise_write took `namespace: str | None = None`
and skipped the check whenever the value was falsy, so three distinct things
collapsed into one permissive case: "no namespace dimension", "scope unknown",
and "deliberately every namespace".

The sharpest instance was vulnerability suppression. _entry_namespace returned
a namespace only for an entry pinned to exactly one, so a cluster-wide entry
(no namespaces) and a multi-namespace entry both returned None and went
unchecked -- naming MORE namespaces bought LESS enforcement. A server set to
NV_ALLOWED_NAMESPACES=staging could hide a CVE across the whole cluster.

Fourteen further call sites omitted the argument entirely and inherited the
default silently, among them nv_delete_group, the WAF and DLP sensor
update/delete tools, and the whole-profile vulnerability replace.

Changes:

- guard: `namespace` is now REQUIRED and accepts a name, a sequence of names,
  CLUSTER_WIDE, or None. Omitting it is a TypeError, not a silent pass.
- New NV_ALLOW_CLUSTER_WIDE (default false), consulted only when an allowlist
  is set: a cluster-wide mutation is refused rather than waved through for
  lack of a namespace to check.
- A sequence scope requires EVERY name to be inside the allowlist.
- _entry_namespace reports CLUSTER_WIDE for an unpinned entry and the full
  tuple for a multi-namespace one; _entries_namespace does the same for the
  whole-profile replace.
- Seven cluster-scoped operations moved from None to CLUSTER_WIDE:
  nv_apply_system_request, nv_set_namespace_defaults, nv_update_system_config,
  nv_update_scan_config, nv_delete_all_network_rules,
  nv_delete_all_admission_rules, nv_set_admission_state.
- None is now reserved for objects with genuinely no namespace dimension, and
  every such site says why.

test_apply_system_request_ignores_namespace_allowlist pinned the old bypass
and its docstring asked to be the test that fails once the guard could scope
the call. It did; it is replaced by a refusal test plus an opt-in test.

No behaviour change for a server that sets no allowlist, which includes the
deployed one -- the guard still short-circuits on an empty allowlist.

Also refreshes uv.lock, which still recorded 1.1.0 after the 1.1.2 release.

3. Same question for any tool listing sigstore VERIFIERS (`/v1/scan/sigstore/root_of_trust/{root}/verifier`) — what envelope key does it expect?

content.text:
## 1. The list tool

`nv_list_sigstore_roots` — `/Users/rashford/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/neuvector-mcp/src/neuvector_mcp/tools/sigstore.py:235` (registered via `@mcp.tool(name="nv_list_sigstore_roots", ...)` at line 230).

## 2. Extraction code

The tool body (sigstore.py:247-249):

```python
        app = app_context(ctx)
        body = await app.client.request("GET", "/v1/scan/sigstore/root_of_trust")
        items = _unwrap_list(body, ROOTS_KEY)
```

with the constant at sigstore.py:87 and the helper at sigstore.py:92-104:

```python
ROOTS_KEY = "roots_of_trust"
...
def _unwrap_list(body: Any, key: str) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    """Return the object list from either ``{key: [...]}`` or a bare ``[...]``.

    See :data:`ROOTS_KEY` for why both shapes are accepted.
    """
    items: Any = None
    if isinstance(body, dict):
        items = body.get(key)
    elif isinstance(body, list):
        items = body
    if not isinstance(items, list):
        return []
    return [item for item in items if isinstance(item, dict)]
```

Answer: it expects **`body["roots_of_trust"]` first, and falls back to a bare array**. Both shapes work. Handed the live 5.6.0 `{"roots_of_trust": []}` it returns `[]` correctly (an genuinely empty collection, not a silent parse failure); handed `{"roots_of_trust": [ {...} ]}` it returns the roots. **No breakage, no false-empty.** The only way it silently returns empty is if the controller used some *third* key (neither `roots_of_trust` nor a bare array) — not the case here.

Note the non-dict filter on the last line: any non-object element is dropped silently, and `page.returned` counts only surviving dicts.

## 3. Verifiers list tool

`nv_list_sigstore_verifiers` — sigstore.py:307 (decorator at 302). Extraction at sigstore.py:329-332:

```python
        body = await app.client.request(
            "GET", f"/v1/scan/sigstore/root_of_trust/{root_name}/verifier"
        )
        items = _unwrap_list(body, VERIFIERS_KEY)
```

Envelope key constant, sigstore.py:88-89:

```python
#: Same, for apis.go ``REST_SigstoreVerifierCollection.Verifiers``.
VERIFIERS_KEY = "verifiers"
```

Same dual-shape tolerance: `{"verifiers": [...]}` or a bare array.

There is also a third, different unwrapper for the single-root GET, `_unwrap_root` (sigstore.py:107-122), used by `nv_get_sigstore_root` at line 294. It tries the **bare object first** (`if "name" in body: return body`) and falls back to a `root_of_trust` envelope. Consequence: a wrapped-but-nameless payload, or a root object whose `name` was omitted, yields `{}` and raises `NotFoundError` (line 296).

## 4. The apis.go-vs-apis.yaml comment

sigstore.py:81-89 — this is the explicit discussion:

```python
#: Envelope key of the root-of-trust collection. apis.go
#: ``REST_SigstoreRootOfTrustCollection.RootsOfTrust`` carries
#: ``json:"roots_of_trust"``; apis.yaml declares the same definition as a bare
#: array. apis.go wins (house rule), but the readers below accept either shape:
#: the disagreement cannot be settled offline and guessing wrong would turn a
#: successful read into an empty list, which reads as "no roots configured".
ROOTS_KEY = "roots_of_trust"
#: Same, for apis.go ``REST_SigstoreVerifierCollection.Verifiers``.
VERIFIERS_KEY = "verifiers"
```

And the parallel note for the single-root case, sigstore.py:110-115: apis.yaml declares the 200 schema as a bare `REST_SigstoreRootOfTrust_GET` and apis.go defines no wrapper struct, "so the bare object is the documented shape and is tried first."

## 5. Test mocks

`/Users/rashford/Library/Mobile Documents/com~apple~CloudDocs/Developer/neuvector-mcp/tests/test_sigstore.py`

- Line 76 — wrapped, populated: `nv_mock.get(ROOTS_PATH).respond(200, json={"roots_of_trust": [ROOT_RAW]})`

- Line 107 — wrapped, empty (the exact live 5.6.0 shape): `nv_mock.get(ROOTS_PATH).respond(200, json={"roots_of_trust": []})` in `test_list_sigstore_roots_empty_means_no_verification`, asserting `structured_content["roots_of_trust"] == []` and `page.returned == 0`.
- Line 114 — single root, bare object: `nv_mock.get(ROOT_PATH).respond(200, json=ROOT_RAW)`; line 126 mocks `json={}` to assert `NotFoundError`.
- Line 135 — verifiers, wrapped only: `nv_mock.get(VERIFIERS_PATH).respond(200, json={"verifiers": [VERIFIER_RAW]})`

`ROOT_RAW` (lines 50-60) itself embeds a nested `"verifiers": [VERIFIER_RAW]` list, so the roots-list projection is exercised with nested verifiers.

Coverage gap worth noting: there is a bare-array test for **roots** (line 91) but **no** equivalent bare-array test for `nv_list_sigstore_verifiers` — the `_unwrap_list` fallback path is only proven through the roots route, even though both tools share the helper.
